name: Fermat's Little Theorem
original_full_statement: Let p be a prime number and let a be an integer. If a is not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) is congruent to 1 modulo p.
hypotheses: p is a prime number
a is an integer
a is not divisible by p
conclusion: a^(p-1) is congruent to 1 modulo p

name: Euler's Theorem
original_full_statement: If n is a positive integer and a is an integer coprime to n, then a^phi(n) is congruent to 1 modulo n, where phi is Euler's totient function.
hypotheses: n is a positive integer
a is an integer
the greatest common divisor of a and n is 1
conclusion: a^phi(n) is congruent to 1 modulo n

name: Lagrange's Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup of G, then the order of H divides the order of G.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
H is a subgroup of G
conclusion: The order of H divides the order of G

name: Cauchy's Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a finite group and p is a prime number that divides the order of G, then G contains an element of order p.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
p is a prime number
p divides the order of G
conclusion: G contains an element of order p

name: Wedderburn's Little Theorem
original_full_statement: Every finite division ring is a commutative field.
hypotheses: R is a division ring
R is finite
conclusion: R is commutative

name: Finite Integral Domain Theorem
original_full_statement: Every finite integral domain is a field.
hypotheses: R is an integral domain
R is finite
conclusion: R is a field

name: Cyclic Multiplicative Subgroup Theorem
original_full_statement: Any finite subgroup of the multiplicative group of a field is cyclic.
hypotheses: F is a field
G is a finite subgroup of the multiplicative group of F
conclusion: G is a cyclic group

name: Primitive Element Theorem
original_full_statement: Every finite, separable field extension is generated by a single element.
hypotheses: E is a finite field extension of F
E is a separable extension of F
conclusion: There exists an element alpha in E such that E = F(alpha)

name: Index 2 Subgroup Theorem
original_full_statement: If H is a subgroup of a group G such that the index [G:H] is 2, then H is a normal subgroup of G.
hypotheses: G is a group
H is a subgroup of G
The index [G:H] is exactly 2
conclusion: H is a normal subgroup of G

name: Center of a p-group Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a finite group of order p^n where p is a prime and n >= 1, then the center of G is non-trivial.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
The order of G is p^n for some prime p and integer n >= 1
conclusion: The center Z(G) is non-trivial

name: Maximal Ideal Quotient Theorem
original_full_statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity 1 != 0. An ideal M of R is maximal if and only if the quotient ring R/M is a field.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with identity 1 != 0
M is a maximal ideal of R
conclusion: The quotient ring R/M is a field

name: PID implies UFD Theorem
original_full_statement: Every principal ideal domain (PID) is a unique factorization domain (UFD).
hypotheses: R is a principal ideal domain
conclusion: R is a unique factorization domain

name: Boolean Ring Commutativity Theorem
original_full_statement: If R is a ring in which x^2 = x for all x in R, then R is commutative.
hypotheses: R is a ring
For every element x in R, x^2 = x
conclusion: R is a commutative ring

name: Tower Law for Field Extensions
original_full_statement: Let F, K, and L be fields such that F is a subfield of K and K is a subfield of L. If [K:F] and [L:K] are finite, then [L:F] is finite and [L:F] = [L:K][K:F].
hypotheses: F, K, and L are fields
F is a subfield of K
K is a subfield of L
The extension K over F is finite
The extension L over K is finite
conclusion: The extension L over F is finite and the degree [L:F] equals the product [L:K] * [K:F]

name: Wilson's Theorem
original_full_statement: An integer p > 1 is a prime number if and only if (p-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo p.
hypotheses: p is a prime number
conclusion: (p-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo p

name: Chinese Remainder Theorem (Two Moduli)
original_full_statement: Let m and n be positive integers such that gcd(m, n) = 1. For any integers a and b, there exists an integer x such that x is congruent to a modulo m and x is congruent to b modulo n. Furthermore, x is unique modulo mn.
hypotheses: m and n are positive integers
The greatest common divisor of m and n is 1
a and b are integers
conclusion: There exists an integer x, unique modulo mn, such that x is congruent to a modulo m and x is congruent to b modulo n

name: Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a finite group acting on a set X. For any element x in X, the order of G is equal to the size of the orbit of x multiplied by the order of the stabilizer of x.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
X is a set
G acts on the set X
x is an element of X
conclusion: The order of G is equal to the product of the cardinality of the orbit of x and the order of the stabilizer of x.

name: Prime Ideal Quotient Theorem
original_full_statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity, and let I be a proper ideal of R. Then the quotient ring R/I is an integral domain if and only if I is a prime ideal.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with identity
I is a proper ideal of R
conclusion: The quotient ring R/I is an integral domain if and only if I is a prime ideal.

name: Finite Extension implies Algebraic Extension
original_full_statement: If E is a finite extension of a field F, then E is an algebraic extension of F.
hypotheses: F is a field
E is a field extension of F
The degree of the extension [E:F] is finite
conclusion: Every element of E is algebraic over F.

name: Euclid's Lemma
original_full_statement: If a prime p divides the product of two integers a and b, then p must divide a or p must divide b.
hypotheses: p is a prime number
a and b are integers
p divides the product ab
conclusion: p divides a or p divides b.

name: First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
original_full_statement: Let G and H be groups, and let f: G -> H be a group homomorphism. Then the quotient group G/ker(f) is isomorphic to the image of f.
hypotheses: G and H are groups
f is a function from G to H
f is a group homomorphism
conclusion: The quotient group G/ker(f) is isomorphic to the image of f.

name: Euclidean Domain implies Principal Ideal Domain
original_full_statement: Every Euclidean domain is a principal ideal domain.
hypotheses: R is an integral domain
R is a Euclidean domain
conclusion: Every ideal of R is generated by a single element, making R a principal ideal domain.

name: First Supplement to the Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
original_full_statement: For an odd prime p, -1 is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if p is congruent to 1 modulo 4.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime number
conclusion: -1 is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if p is congruent to 1 modulo 4.

name: Polynomial Ring over a UFD is a UFD
original_full_statement: If R is a unique factorization domain, then the polynomial ring R[x] is also a unique factorization domain.
hypotheses: R is a unique factorization domain
conclusion: The polynomial ring R[x] is a unique factorization domain.

name: Subgroups of a Cyclic Group Theorem
original_full_statement: Every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic.
hypotheses: Let G be a cyclic group
Let H be a subgroup of G
conclusion: H is a cyclic group

name: Characteristic of an Integral Domain Theorem
original_full_statement: The characteristic of an integral domain is either 0 or a prime number.
hypotheses: Let R be an integral domain
Let c be the characteristic of R
Assume c is not equal to 0
conclusion: c is a prime number

name: Linear Diophantine Equation Solvability Theorem
original_full_statement: The linear Diophantine equation ax + by = c has integer solutions if and only if the greatest common divisor of a and b divides c.
hypotheses: Let a, b, and c be integers
Let d be the greatest common divisor of a and b
conclusion: The equation ax + by = c has integer solutions for x and y if and only if d divides c

name: Finite Field Order Theorem
original_full_statement: The order of any finite field is a prime power.
hypotheses: Let F be a finite field
conclusion: The cardinality of F is p^n for some prime number p and positive integer n

name: Direct Product of Coprime Cyclic Groups Theorem
original_full_statement: The direct product of two cyclic groups of orders m and n is cyclic if and only if m and n are coprime.
hypotheses: Let m and n be positive integers
Assume the greatest common divisor of m and n is 1
conclusion: The direct product of the cyclic group of order m and the cyclic group of order n is isomorphic to the cyclic group of order mn

name: Polynomial Roots over a Field Theorem
original_full_statement: A non-zero polynomial of degree n over a field has at most n distinct roots in that field.
hypotheses: Let F be a field
Let f(x) be a non-zero polynomial in the polynomial ring F[x]
Let n be the degree of f(x)
conclusion: The polynomial f(x) has at most n distinct roots in F

name: Fermat's Theorem on Sums of Two Squares
original_full_statement: An odd prime p can be expressed as the sum of two integer squares if and only if p is congruent to 1 modulo 4.
hypotheses: Let p be a prime number
Assume p is an odd prime
conclusion: p can be expressed as the sum of two integer squares if and only if p is congruent to 1 modulo 4

name: Degree of a Simple Algebraic Extension Theorem
original_full_statement: If alpha is algebraic over F, then the degree of the simple extension F(alpha) over F is equal to the degree of the minimal polynomial of alpha over F.
hypotheses: Let E be a field extension of a field F
Let alpha be an element of E that is algebraic over F
Let m(x) be the minimal polynomial of alpha over F
conclusion: The degree of the field extension F(alpha) over F is equal to the degree of the polynomial m(x)

name: Quotient by Center Cyclic Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a group such that the quotient group G/Z(G) is cyclic, then G is abelian.
hypotheses: Let G be a group.
Let Z(G) be the center of G.
The quotient group G/Z(G) is a cyclic group.
conclusion: G is an abelian group.

name: Sylow's Third Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a finite group of order n = p^k m, where p is a prime not dividing m. Then the number of Sylow p-subgroups, n_p, divides m and satisfies n_p ≡ 1 (mod p).
hypotheses: Let G be a finite group of order n.
Let p be a prime number dividing n.
Let n = p^k * m where k is a positive integer and p does not divide m.
Let n_p be the number of Sylow p-subgroups of G.
conclusion: n_p divides m and n_p is congruent to 1 modulo p.

name: Eisenstein's Criterion
original_full_statement: Let f(x) = a_n x^n + ... + a_0 be a polynomial with integer coefficients. If there exists a prime p such that p divides a_i for all i < n, p does not divide a_n, and p^2 does not divide a_0, then f(x) is irreducible over the rational numbers.
hypotheses: Let f(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_1 x + a_0 be a polynomial in Z[x] with degree n >= 1.
Let p be a prime number.
p divides a_i for all integers i such that 0 <= i < n.
p does not divide a_n.
p^2 does not divide a_0.
conclusion: f(x) is irreducible over the field of rational numbers Q.

name: Field Ideals Theorem
original_full_statement: A commutative ring with identity 1 ≠ 0 is a field if and only if its only ideals are {0} and the ring itself.
hypotheses: Let R be a commutative ring with identity.
The identity element 1 is not equal to the zero element 0 in R.
The only ideals of R are the zero ideal {0} and R itself.
conclusion: R is a field.

name: Galois Group of a Finite Field Theorem
original_full_statement: The Galois group of a finite extension of a finite field is cyclic and generated by the Frobenius automorphism.
hypotheses: Let F_p be a finite field with p elements, where p is a prime number.
Let F_{p^n} be a finite field extension of F_p of degree n.
conclusion: The Galois group Gal(F_{p^n} / F_p) is a cyclic group of order n generated by the Frobenius automorphism.

name: Euler's Criterion
original_full_statement: Let p be an odd prime and a be an integer coprime to p. Then a is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if a^((p-1)/2) ≡ 1 (mod p).
hypotheses: Let p be an odd prime number.
Let a be an integer.
a is coprime to p.
conclusion: a is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if a^((p-1)/2) is congruent to 1 modulo p.

name: Second Supplement to the Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
original_full_statement: For an odd prime p, 2 is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod 8) or p ≡ 7 (mod 8).
hypotheses: Let p be an odd prime number.
conclusion: 2 is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if p is congruent to 1 or 7 modulo 8.

name: Alternating Group Simplicity Theorem
original_full_statement: The alternating group A_n is simple for all n >= 5.
hypotheses: Let n be an integer.
n is greater than or equal to 5.
Let A_n be the alternating group on n letters.
conclusion: A_n is a simple group.

name: Sylow's First Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a finite group and p be a prime number. If p^k divides the order of G for some non-negative integer k, then G has a subgroup of order p^k.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
p is a prime number
k is a non-negative integer
p^k divides the order of G
conclusion: G has a subgroup of order p^k

name: Burnside's Lemma
original_full_statement: Let G be a finite group acting on a finite set X. The number of distinct orbits of this action is equal to the average number of points fixed by the elements of G.
hypotheses: G is a finite group
X is a finite set
G acts on the set X
conclusion: The number of orbits of the action of G on X is equal to (1/|G|) * sum_{g in G} |X^g|, where X^g is the set of elements in X fixed by g

name: Nilradical Ideal Theorem
original_full_statement: In a commutative ring, the set of all nilpotent elements forms an ideal.
hypotheses: R is a ring
R is commutative
conclusion: The set of all nilpotent elements of R is an ideal of R

name: Units of a Polynomial Ring over an Integral Domain
original_full_statement: If R is an integral domain, then the group of units of the polynomial ring R[x] is exactly the group of units of R.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with identity
R is an integral domain
conclusion: The units of the polynomial ring R[x] are exactly the units of R

name: Transitivity of Algebraic Extensions
original_full_statement: If L is an algebraic field extension of K, and M is an algebraic field extension of L, then M is an algebraic field extension of K.
hypotheses: K, L, and M are fields
L is an extension field of K
M is an extension field of L
L is an algebraic extension of K
M is an algebraic extension of L
conclusion: M is an algebraic extension of K

name: Uniqueness of Splitting Fields
original_full_statement: Any two splitting fields of a non-constant polynomial over a field F are isomorphic via an isomorphism that fixes F pointwise.
hypotheses: F is a field
f(x) is a non-constant polynomial in F[x]
K1 is a splitting field of f(x) over F
K2 is a splitting field of f(x) over F
conclusion: There exists a field isomorphism from K1 to K2 that is the identity map on F

name: Multiplicativity of Euler's Totient Function
original_full_statement: If m and n are coprime positive integers, then Euler's totient function satisfies phi(mn) = phi(m)phi(n).
hypotheses: m is a positive integer
n is a positive integer
m and n are coprime
conclusion: phi(mn) = phi(m)phi(n), where phi is Euler's totient function

name: Rational Root Theorem
original_full_statement: If a rational number p/q in lowest terms is a root of a polynomial with integer coefficients, then p divides the constant term and q divides the leading coefficient.
hypotheses: f(x) = a_n x^n + ... + a_0 is a polynomial
The coefficients of f(x) are integers
a_n is non-zero
p and q are coprime integers
q is non-zero
p/q is a root of f(x)
conclusion: p divides a_0 and q divides a_n

name: Cayley's Theorem
original_full_statement: Every group is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group acting on itself.
hypotheses: Let G be a group.
conclusion: G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group Sym(G).

name: Sylow's Second Theorem
original_full_statement: Any two Sylow p-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate.
hypotheses: Let G be a finite group.
Let p be a prime number.
Let P and Q be Sylow p-subgroups of G.
conclusion: There exists an element g in G such that Q = g P g^(-1).

name: Gauss's Lemma for Primitive Polynomials
original_full_statement: The product of two primitive polynomials over a unique factorization domain is also a primitive polynomial.
hypotheses: Let R be a unique factorization domain.
Let f(x) and g(x) be primitive polynomials in the polynomial ring R[x].
conclusion: The product f(x)g(x) is a primitive polynomial in R[x].

name: Dedekind's Theorem on Linear Independence of Characters
original_full_statement: Any set of distinct field homomorphisms from a field E to a field F is linearly independent over F.
hypotheses: Let E and F be fields.
Let S be a finite set of distinct field homomorphisms from E to F.
conclusion: The homomorphisms in S are linearly independent over F in the vector space of functions from E to F.

name: Derived Subgroup Quotient Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a group, H be a normal subgroup of G, and G' be the commutator subgroup of G. The quotient group G/H is abelian if and only if G' is contained in H.
hypotheses: G is a group
H is a normal subgroup of G
G' is the commutator subgroup of G
conclusion: The quotient group G/H is abelian if and only if G' is a subgroup of H

name: Perfect Field Characteristic Zero Theorem
original_full_statement: Let F be a field. If the characteristic of F is 0, then every irreducible polynomial over F is separable, and consequently F is a perfect field.
hypotheses: F is a field
The characteristic of F is 0
conclusion: Every irreducible polynomial over F is separable, and F is a perfect field

name: Legendre's Formula
original_full_statement: For any prime p and any positive integer n, the p-adic valuation of n! is the sum over k >= 1 of the floor of n/(p^k).
hypotheses: Let n be a positive integer.
Let p be a prime number.
conclusion: The p-adic valuation of n! is equal to the sum from k=1 to infinity of the floor of n/(p^k).

name: First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings
original_full_statement: Let R and S be rings, and let f: R -> S be a ring homomorphism. Then the kernel of f is an ideal of R, and the image of f is isomorphic to the quotient ring R / ker(f).
hypotheses: R and S are rings
f is a ring homomorphism from R to S
conclusion: The kernel of f is an ideal of R, and the quotient ring R / ker(f) is isomorphic to the image of f

name: Lucas' Theorem
original_full_statement: For non-negative integers m and n and a prime p, the binomial coefficient C(m, n) is congruent modulo p to the product of the binomial coefficients C(m_i, n_i), where m_i and n_i are the digits of m and n in base p.
hypotheses: p is a prime number
m and n are non-negative integers
m_i and n_i are the coefficients of the base p expansions of m and n respectively
conclusion: The binomial coefficient C(m, n) is congruent to the product of C(m_i, n_i) modulo p

name: Gauss's Lemma for Polynomials
original_full_statement: The product of two primitive polynomials over a unique factorization domain is a primitive polynomial.
hypotheses: R is a unique factorization domain
f(x) is a primitive polynomial in R[x]
g(x) is a primitive polynomial in R[x]
conclusion: The product polynomial f(x)g(x) is a primitive polynomial in R[x]

name: Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
original_full_statement: Let p and q be distinct odd prime numbers. Then the product of the Legendre symbols (p/q) and (q/p) is equal to (-1)^(((p-1)/2)*((q-1)/2)).
hypotheses: p is an odd prime number
q is an odd prime number
p and q are distinct
conclusion: The product of the Legendre symbols (p/q) and (q/p) is equal to (-1)^(((p-1)/2)*((q-1)/2))

name: Commutator Subgroup Quotient Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a group and [G,G] be its commutator subgroup. Then [G,G] is a normal subgroup of G, and the quotient group G/[G,G] is abelian. Furthermore, if N is a normal subgroup of G such that G/N is abelian, then [G,G] is a subgroup of N.
hypotheses: G is a group
[G,G] is the commutator subgroup of G generated by all commutators aba^{-1}b^{-1} for a,b in G
conclusion: [G,G] is a normal subgroup of G, the quotient group G/[G,G] is abelian, and any normal subgroup N yielding an abelian quotient G/N contains [G,G].

name: Splitting Field Existence Theorem
original_full_statement: Let F be a field and let f(x) be a non-constant polynomial in F[x]. Then there exists an extension field K of F such that f(x) splits completely into linear factors in K[x], and K is generated over F by the roots of f(x).
hypotheses: F is a field
f(x) is a non-constant polynomial in the polynomial ring F[x]
conclusion: There exists an extension field K of F that is a splitting field for f(x) over F.

name: Bezout's Identity
original_full_statement: Let a and b be integers, not both zero. Then there exist integers x and y such that ax + by = gcd(a, b).
hypotheses: Let a and b be integers
Let at least one of a or b be non-zero
conclusion: There exist integers x and y such that ax + by is equal to the greatest common divisor of a and b

name: Cyclic Multiplicative Group of a Finite Field
original_full_statement: If F is a finite field, then the multiplicative group of non-zero elements of F is a cyclic group.
hypotheses: F is a finite field
F^\times is the group of non-zero elements of F under multiplication
conclusion: F^\times is a cyclic group.

name: Principal Ideal Domain implies Unique Factorization Domain
original_full_statement: Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain.
hypotheses: Let R be an integral domain
Let every ideal in R be generated by a single element
conclusion: R is a Unique Factorization Domain

name: Subfields of a Finite Field Theorem
original_full_statement: Let F be a finite field of order p^n, where p is a prime and n >= 1. For every positive integer k, F contains exactly one subfield of order p^k if k divides n, and no subfield of order p^k otherwise.
hypotheses: F is a finite field
The order of F is p^n for some prime p and integer n >= 1
k is a positive integer
conclusion: F contains exactly one subfield of order p^k if k divides n, and contains no subfield of order p^k if k does not divide n.

name: Subring Test
original_full_statement: A non-empty subset S of a ring R is a subring if and only if it is closed under subtraction and multiplication.
hypotheses: R is a ring
S is a non-empty subset of R
For all a and b in S, the difference a - b is in S
For all a and b in S, the product ab is in S
conclusion: S is a subring of R

name: Lattice Isomorphism Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a group and N be a normal subgroup of G. There is a bijection between the set of subgroups of G containing N and the set of subgroups of the quotient group G/N.
hypotheses: G is a group
N is a normal subgroup of G
conclusion: There is a bijection between the set of subgroups of G containing N and the set of subgroups of the quotient group G/N

name: Division Algorithm for Polynomials
original_full_statement: Let F be a field and let f(x) and g(x) be polynomials in F[x] with g(x) not the zero polynomial. Then there exist unique polynomials q(x) and r(x) in F[x] such that f(x) = q(x)g(x) + r(x) and either r(x) = 0 or \deg(r(x)) < \deg(g(x)).
hypotheses: Let F be a field.
Let f(x) and g(x) be polynomials in F[x].
g(x) is not the zero polynomial.
conclusion: There exist unique polynomials q(x) and r(x) in F[x] such that f(x) = q(x)g(x) + r(x) and either r(x) = 0 or \deg(r(x)) < \deg(g(x)).

name: Multiple Roots Theorem
original_full_statement: Let F be a field and f(x) be a non-constant polynomial in F[x]. Then f(x) has a multiple root in some extension field of F if and only if f(x) and its formal derivative f'(x) share a common factor of degree greater than or equal to 1 in F[x].
hypotheses: F is a field
f(x) is a non-constant polynomial in F[x]
conclusion: f(x) has a multiple root in some extension field of F if and only if f(x) and its formal derivative f'(x) share a common factor of degree greater than or equal to 1 in F[x].

name: Finite Subgroup of a Field Multiplicative Group Theorem
original_full_statement: Any finite subgroup of the multiplicative group of a field is cyclic.
hypotheses: F is a field
F^* is the multiplicative group of non-zero elements of F
G is a finite subgroup of F^*
conclusion: G is a cyclic group
